THIRD, non-overlapping window (2025-12-15..2026-03-14, 240-150d ago) for the SHIPPED DEFAULT params flagged as 'noise, needs a 3rd window' in Run 2 (that run scored OOS PF 1.903/120 trades on the 60-0d window despite train PF 0.472). FIRST DCA-specific evaluation (new methodology this run: run_dca_backtest has no round-trip trades, so PF/trade-count bar does not apply -- instead compared capital-normalized ROI (unrealized_pnl/invested %) of the SHIPPED DEFAULT dip-buy feature vs a flat fixed-schedule baseline, across 3 non-overlapping windows x 8 symbols, same anchors as candle-strategy research: train=2026-03-14..2026-06-12 (win 6/8 symbols, +0.26pp ROI), test=2026-06-12..2026-08-11 (win 2/8, -0.07pp ROI, essentially noise), plus a 3rd older window 2025-12-15..2026-03-14 (win 8/8, +0.61pp ROI). Mixed across windows -- does NOT clear a majority-of-symbols win in the trending-up test window, so not a clean unconditional edge by this research programs own anti-noise standard. But mechanism is explicable (extra buys land at locally-lower 24h-dip prices by construction, so it can only help when dips occur and is a no-op, not a loss, when they dont) -- consistent with 2/3 windows meaningfully positive and the 3rd being near-zero rather than negative. Already the shipped default; this run VALIDATES keeping it as-is, does not argue for a change either direction.

More aggressive dip-buy variant (threshold 5%->3%, multiplier 1.5x->2.5x) vs the shipped default, same 3-window DCA ROI methodology (see sibling entry). Beats shipped default on ROI in older window (8/8 symbols, +1.72pp) and train window (7/8, +0.55pp) but only 4/8 (50%, +0.09pp, noise-level) in the trending-up test window -- not a clean 3/3-window win. Also deploys 13-30% MORE total capital than the default across symbols (more dip events trigger at the lower threshold) -- a real practical capital/liquidity requirement and larger concentration of exposure into still-declining assets, not free even though the per-dollar ROI compares fairly. Given the borderline test-window result and the added capital/risk footprint, NOT adopted as new default -- would need a cleaner win in a genuinely trending-up window before justifying more aggressive dip-buying as the shipped default.

Run 5: DCA schedule-interval sweep (hourly/daily/weekly), first-ever variation of `interval` (prior DCA runs only varied dip_* params, always daily). Compared hourly's capital-normalized ROI vs the shipped daily baseline, same param set otherwise (both flat and dip_default variants), across 3 non-overlapping windows x 8 symbols (16 pairs/window). Older window: +0.11pp avg, 87.5% symbol-win. Train: +0.06pp avg, 93.8% win. Test (trending-up): -0.03pp avg, 43.8% win -- sign flips, and the magnitude is trivial (<=0.11pp, i.e. cents on $100) in every window. Mechanically expected: hourly just finely re-slices the same total buying period daily already covers, so average purchase price barely moves -- there's no reason more granular scheduling should change expected cost basis, and the data confirms that (noise-level deltas, inconsistent sign). Also has a real operational cost not captured by ROI: 2160 buy events per symbol per 90d window vs 90 for daily -- 24x more live orders/fees-per-notional-dollar risk (below-minimum-notional issues, API load) for zero measurable benefit. Verdict: noise, reject switching the default off daily.

Run 5: same interval-sweep methodology as the hourly sibling entry. Weekly vs shipped daily baseline: older window -1.10pp avg ROI delta, 0/16 (0%) symbol-variant pairs beat daily; train -0.29pp, 31.2% win; test (trending-up) -0.61pp, 25% win. Unlike hourly, weekly is systematically worse in every one of the 3 windows -- never even approaches a majority win, and its one best window (train) is still a loss, not a wash. Mechanism: weekly fires only ~10-14 times per 90d window on a single fixed weekday/time, so each buy is a much larger lump and the schedule samples a far less representative slice of the window's price path than daily's 90 buys -- more exposure to single-draw timing luck, and the data shows that luck ran negative in all 3 independent windows, not just the down-trending ones (i.e. this isn't the same 'helps-in-declines, neutral-in-uptrends' pattern seen with dip-buying -- weekly has no offsetting upside anywhere). Verdict: reject -- do not offer weekly as a recommended interval; no evidence it's ever better and consistent evidence it's worse.

Run 8: 3rd-ranked flatten_on_stop=True 4h combo. Wider range (10%) at 13 levels -- worse than the 6%/13-level combo on both PF and account return (train ret -0.235% vs -0.060%), consistent with the range-pct sweep at 1h/15m: wider ranges dilute per-level fill frequency without offsetting benefit.

Run 8: worst of the 4 flatten_on_stop=True 4h combos (widest range + fewest levels = coarsest, most whipsaw-prone ladder). Train PF 0.308 (worst), OOS PF 0.355 (worst) -- confirms narrower range / more levels is directionally better within this family, though none clear breakeven.

Run 8: flatten_on_stop=False structural artifact, not a signal -- a grid sell only ever fires ABOVE its paired buy, so every closed trade is a win by construction (100% win rate, trade-PF undefined/infinite) regardless of whether the strategy is actually profitable; unrealized losses on held inventory never show up in trade PF at all, only in the account-level return (avg_ret_pct, mark-to-market). That real return is train -0.90% (a real loss the trade-level PF completely hides) vs test +0.16% -- sign flips between windows exactly like unhedged directional spot exposure would, because with no flatten that's what unflattened grid inventory effectively is. PF is meaningless here; logged as noise, not a candidate.

Run 8: same flatten_on_stop=False PF-artifact pattern as the sibling 6%/8-level entry (see that rationale for the mechanism). Real account return train -0.68% vs test +0.16% -- same train-loses/test-gains flip-flop, same regime-luck signature, not an edge.

Run 8: same flatten_on_stop=False PF-artifact pattern (see 6%/8-level entry for mechanism). Real account return train -0.80% vs test +0.16% -- same flip-flop. Also the smallest train sample (18 trades) of the whole grid, wide range x few levels fires rarely.

Run 8: same flatten_on_stop=False PF-artifact pattern (see 6%/8-level entry for mechanism). Largest swing of the whole grid: train -1.01% (worst real train loss of any combo this run) vs test +0.39% (best real test return of any combo this run) -- the most extreme version of the train-loses/test-gains flip, underscoring that this is regime direction, not strategy skill; wider range + more levels just means more capital riding the same unhedged directional exposure.

Run 10: BASELINE (no ADX gate) for the range=10.0%/levels=13 flatten_on_stop=True 1h grid config, on a fresh non-overlapping window (train 2026-03-18..2026-06-16, test 2026-06-16..2026-08-15 -- 4 days later than Run 2/8's anchors). Logged as the reference point for the ADX-gated variants below, not a new candidate on its own (already-closed family).

Run 10: FIRST test of an ADX(14) trend-strength gate on grid -- the 'genuinely new signal design' flagged as the priority next step since Run 8 (distilled learnings: grid is a directional bet in disguise, would need a range-detection filter to reopen). Implemented as a pure addition on top of the existing stop_outside_range/flatten_on_stop mechanism (unchanged): new grid buys are skipped on any candle where ADX(14) >= 30 (blocks entries only while the market shows strong trend strength; sells/pause/flatten logic untouched). Tested as a research-only script (not merged into grid.py/simulator.py -- see research/experiments/adx_grid_gate.py), range=10.0% levels=13, same window as the sibling no-gate baseline. Result: gating REDUCES trade count (101 vs 124 baseline) but does not improve PF -- train 0.214 / test 0.234 vs baseline train 0.285 / test 0.285 -- flat or modestly worse at every threshold tested (30/25/20/15), never better. Mechanistically explicable: the existing wide auto-range (6-10%) already tolerates real intra-range volatility, so grid's losses come from ordinary in-range chop and the eventual out-of-range exit, not specifically from high-ADX periods -- by the time ADX(14) elevates, price has typically already left the range and stop_outside_range has already fired, making the ADX gate redundant with a mechanism that's already there.

Run 12: FIRST 5m pass for trend_momentum -- last untested TF for this family (4h/1h/15m already closed, no edge, Runs 1/3/7). Top-ranked (highest train PF) of a 12-combo grid (3 EMA pairs x 2 rsi_buy_min x 2 require_macd, same shape as Run 7's 15m grid) using the shipped-default EMA pair (20/50). Train PF 0.211 (real sample, 29 trades, just under the 30-trade floor) collapses further OOS to PF 0.028/42 trades (real sample) -- the single worst result of any trend_momentum TF tested, decisively negative in both windows with no train/test ambiguity. Sharply fewer entries than 15m's same-pair combo (29 vs 141 train trades) despite 5m having far more candles per window -- consistent with the 3%-daily-loss halt tripping early and often at 5m (SL 2%/TP 4% vs candle noise fires stop-losses in rapid daily clusters, each cluster halting new entries for the rest of that UTC day) rather than the EMA cross itself becoming rarer. Confirms the standing pattern: faster TF = worse for this family, not better -- consistent with, and now the clean tail-end of, the '1m catastrophic, 15m worst-but-tested, 1h/4h least-bad-but-still-no-edge' TF ordering already established. trend_momentum is now grid-searched with train/test rigor at every TF from 5m to 4h -- no edge anywhere; only 1m (known catastrophic, never worth re-testing) and 1d (untested, low priority) remain.

Run 13: FIRST 5m pass for grid -- last untested TF for this family (15m/1h/4h already closed, no edge, Runs 2/8; both ADX-gate attempts for grid and trend_momentum also closed as no-improvement/noise, Runs 10-11, so no ADX gating repeated here). Config mirrors Run 2/8 exactly (range=10%, levels=13, flatten_on_stop=True, quote_per_level=150) for direct cross-TF comparability, using unmodified production run_grid_backtest. Hypothesis going in: grid's range math operates on price levels not candle count, so finer TF changes fill sampling precision without necessarily worsening the mechanism the way it does for trend_momentum/mean_reversion (daily-halt interaction, signal noise) -- worth testing rather than assuming. Result: train PF 0.848 (real sample, 199 trades) already <1, collapsing further to test PF 0.228 (real sample, 106 trades) -- decisively negative both windows, no train/test ambiguity. Real (not small-sample) rejection: the hypothesis that 5m's finer sampling would help was wrong -- likely because tighter time resolution means the SAME price excursion crosses grid levels in and out repeatedly within noisy micro-moves, generating more low-quality round-trips (visible in the unusually high 77% win rate on train that still nets PF<1: many tiny wins, a few large losses when price finally breaks the range) rather than more genuine range-bound profit-taking.

Run 13: second 5m grid config (range=6%, tighter band, same levels/flatten shape as Run 2/8's range=6 arm). Train PF 0.42 (real sample, 184 trades), test PF 0.343 (real sample, 154 trades) -- decisively negative both windows, consistent with the range=10 sibling above. Tighter range triggers stop_outside_range/flatten more often (more trades touch the boundary sooner on noisy 5m candles), which is directionally why win% is lower here (67% vs 77%) but PF is still worse, not better -- confirms the range=10 result isn't a fluke of that specific width. grid is now grid-searched with train/test rigor at every TF from 5m to 4h -- no edge anywhere; only 1m (known catastrophic pattern from other strategies, not separately tested for grid but not worth testing) and 1d (untested, low priority, same starvation concerns as other families) remain, and neither is expected to change the verdict.

Run 14: NEW DCA variant flagged as open in DISTILLED LEARNINGS after Run 4/5 -- a cap of 5 dip-multiplied buy(s) per backtest window (after the cap, scheduled buys still fire at the flat quote_amount, just without the 1.5x bonus; schedule itself is never skipped). Research-only reimplementation of run_dca_backtest's loop in research/experiments/dca_dip_cap.py (sanity-checked: cap=None reproduces production run_dca_backtest's unrealized_pnl to within float rounding on BTC/train). Compared capital-normalized ROI (unrealized_pnl/invested %) of the capped variant vs the uncapped shipped default, same 3-non-overlapping-window x 8-symbol methodology as Run 4/5, windows shifted to today's anchor (older 2025-12-19..2026-03-19, train 2026-03-19..2026-06-18, test 2026-06-18..2026-08-17). Result: capping the ROI delta vs uncapped is train -0.0177pp (0/8 symbols, i.e. EVERY symbol worse or equal, 27 real dip-buy events fired in the uncapped baseline this window), test +0.0000pp (0/8 symbols, but this window only saw 3 total dip events across all 8 symbols so the cap essentially never bound -- a tie, not a genuine test). Older reference window (2025-12-19..2026-03-19, not in the train/test protocol fields but same methodology as Run 4/5's 3rd window): -0.2251pp, 0/8 symbols, 56 real dip events -- same direction, larger effect size (more dip events = more room for capping to bite). Mechanism: in a declining/volatile regime, MORE dip-buys (not fewer) mechanically lower the average cost basis further -- capping removes exactly the buys that would have landed at the lowest prices, so it can only ever match or hurt ROI vs the uncapped default, never help. This directly contradicts the original concern (raised when the 2.5x/3% variant was rejected in Run 4) that repeated dip-buying over-concentrates into a falling asset -- the data shows the opposite: more dip-buying in a decline is a benefit (lower cost basis), not a risk, at least at the 1.5x/5% magnitude already shipped. Verdict: reject -- do not cap dip re-buys; the uncapped shipped default remains correct. No code change (research-only script, production dca.py untouched).
